subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should it live as shared approval/elevated/tool-class policy instead of a Telegram-only boolean?
rationale: The requested behavior is absent, but deciding when a chat identity may skip approvals changes a security boundary and config contract that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default shared policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

options.title: Keep existing approval model
options.body: Decline a bypass and document that operators who want fewer prompts should use existing exec/elevated/session approval policy knobs where they already fit.

options.title: Add Telegram-only shortcut
options.body: Implement the proposed Telegram config directly, accepting a smaller patch but higher long-term policy drift risk.

recommendation.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default shared policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product/security approval-boundary and config-surface decision before Telegram and approval owners can safely implement it.
